fieldValues.title: How does waking experience recalibrate a boundary the dreamtime sensed, and what is kept of the difference?
fieldValues.thinking_reached: No option chosen. Raised 2026-11-07 from the owner's words (2ad1b8d8): human and AI sensing differ; a dream-sensed boundary is valid in the dream; waking experience may recalibrate; so we must know where every boundary came from. Nothing has been seen in use yet: srs-context's dream cycle moves records and structure, but no dream has proposed a boundary that a person then moved, so there is no example of the difference.
fieldValues.tensions:
Options, none chosen:
- A. Recalibration is an edit: the waking look replaces the dream boundary; the origin field changes to 'held'. Simplest; loses the difference.
- B. Recalibration is a successor record: the dream boundary stays, the waking one supersedes it; the pair is the evidence of how the two sensings differ. Keeps the difference; the corpus grows.
- C. Recalibration is a relation with a note: one boundary record, with a 'recalibrated-from' relation (or a refines) carrying what moved and why. Keeps the difference in one place; needs a relation type or a convention.
- D. The dream never proposes a boundary, only places to look; every boundary is drawn awake. Avoids the question; contradicts 'dream boundaries are valid'.

Also open: what a dream may do on a dream-sensed boundary before a waking look (exercise 8969754d), and whether the calibration between the two sensings accumulates into something an agent can learn from (the owner: 'I learnt lots from dreams').
fieldValues.unresolved_questions: Whether the difference between a dream boundary and its waking recalibration is the same kind of thing as an affirmation (a judgement relative to a boundary) or something new. Whether a sensed-by-a-person boundary ('this keeps coming back') needs the same treatment as a dream-sensed one.
fieldValues.next_action: Let one dream propose one boundary in a lab repository (the next_steps of the boundary decision), have the owner look at it awake and move it, and record the difference in each of forms A to C to see which reads back usefully.
